body: Apologieze, but I'm not famliar with this algorithm myself, I've not entirely sure that the generated path should be slighty different that a standard AStar (and not just optimize it) that make me wonder whether this is a correct implementation or not.

Hi.
I'm sorry for the delayed response.
The HPA* produces a sub-optimal path by design. It's core functionality is to optimize path fiding in large grids, and does so by dividing the total grid in regions, like dividing a big map of 512 x 512 cells into blocks of 16 x 16 cells. Then, it would perform A* hierarchically. This means, A* will find the best path of those 16 x 16 blocks (the beggining cell being in the first block, and the destiny cell being on the final block of said path). Then, what the algorithm does is exclude all of the blocks that were not choosen by the A* it just ran, and run A* again on a celular level only on the cells containded in the blocks of the choosen block path.
This naturally will not produce the optimal path, but it produces one close enough with alot of optimization for big grids. We tested with a somewhat small grid to see if even when the grid is small we could get some optimization, and we did.

There are somethings that can be improved even further in this issue. Like adding multiple layers instead of just two, or storing some of the block paths found in run time. We thought those are more likely to be a game specific need that not all devs might need, so a simplier implementation would be better for the majority of uses, while still seeing improvments.

Let me know if there is anything else I could clarify.
